text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

After announcing a 22 per cent increase in first-half profits to A$64.5 million yesterday, Adelaide-based conglomerate Southcorp Holdings Ltd revealed it is close to finalising a series of deals to build PET plastic bottle plantS throughout Asia, and saidit is planning on increasing its foreign acquisitions as part of a bid to become a powerhouse in overseas wine and packaging industries. Page 1.

Following talks with the West Australian Government, United States chemical giant Dow Chemical Company has become the latest in a string of contenders trying to gain access to the emerging ethane supply in the State, yesterday signalling its interest in bilding a A$1.5 billion petro-chemical plant. Page 19.

After yesterday posting a A$12.3 million interim net loss, compared with an interim net profit of A$7.4 million in 1996, National Foods managing director Max Ould has defended his plans to turn the company into a pure food beverage group, describing the frst half as a transition period and predicting a strong improvement in earnings and profits in the full-year. Page 19.

Following a trip to Hong Kong, Malaysia and Singapore to assess the markets there for potential ventures and acquisitions, National Foods managing director Max Ould, who has been with the company for six months, says he has cleaned up the food and beverag business' operations enough to set his sights on expanding it. Page 19.

Pacific BBA directors yesterday reported modest rises in revenue and profits for the year to December - net profit for the 1996 calendar year rose six per cent to A$16.9 million - and announced plans to nearly double its capital expenditure to more than A100 million this year, mostly on new factories in the United States and Asia. Page 21.

Despite booking A$1.3 million in retrenchment costs in the December half, which resulted from the company's move to lay off some production workers following a softening in demand for its automotive filters and water pumps, GUD .AX still managed to post a 57 per cent rise in group profit after tax to A$9.13 million. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The all ordinaries index broke a four-session run of outs to finish 10.9 points higher at 2432.1 yesterday amid growing optimism than an accelerating economy will underpin corporate earnings. Investors were responding to better then expected retail trade figures and building approvals. Page 19.

In the first tangible result of BHP's internal review of its steel business, the group has committed to an upgrade of its troubled Glenbrook steelworks facility in New Zealand after local management implemented major job cuts and hopes to cut costs by A$4.6 million a year. Page 19.

After posting a 17 per cent rise in December half net profit to A$62.9 million, a result which puts it on target for a record 1996-97 profit, diversified industrial group Southcorp Holdings Ltd announced it will continue to pursue acquisitions in the wine and packaging sectors. Page 19.

Describing Australia's present corporations law as "out of touch with modern commercial practice", Federal Treasurer Peter Costello announced yesterday the Government will be reviewing the law in an effort to ease the burden on business, while still proteting investors from a repeat of the excesses of the 1980s. Page 19.

After yesterday reporting a A$12.3 million half-yearly loss following a A$25.7 million abnormal write-off relating to redundancy and restructuring, National Foods managing director Max Ould flagged another ownership shake-up of the food industry. Ould sai the acquisition of beverage group Berridale Ltd could be a possibility that will reduce the fixed costs of National's embattled Sunburst juice business. Page 21.

Despite suffering a A$1 million loss on its unsuccessful takeover bid for Azon Ltd, automotive-component and plastics manufacturer Pacific BBA has recorded a 6.1 per cent increase in interim net profit to A$16.8 million. The result is attributed to growin sales from BBA's Asian and North American markets. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following the release of Australian Bureau of Statistics figures yesterday which showed retail trade rose 2.7 per cent after seasonal adjustments in January and a 10.4 per cent increase in building approvals in the same period, Federal Treasurer Peter Cosello reiterated his forecast that economic growth would start to take off. Page 29.

After yesterday posting a 16.6 per cent increase in pre-abnormal items net profit for the six months to December, Southcorp Holdings has predicted double-digit growth for the full-year, underpinned by expected strong performances in its wine and packagingdivisions. Page 29.

Following a combined loss of A$4.5 million and a 6.7 per cent drop in revenue in the September half for its pipelines and products division, buildings materials group James Hardie Industries is looking to quit the Australian pipe business, and is understod to have unofficially put its struggling PVC manufacturing unit on the market last year. Page 29.

Despite suffering a A$36.2 million abnormal loss on a writedown of its assets, sending it to a A$12.3 million loss for the six months to December, Sydney food group National Foods managing director Max Ould said yesterday he was confident of achieving a srong improvement in net profit before abnormals due to cost savings and product development. Page 31.

In a surprise move, Bunge Foods Queensland, the Australian arm of Brazilian commodity giant Bunge Industrial, is to offer A$1.70 for local competitor Defiance Mills' ordinary shares as part of a A$97 million bid for the company. The move is part of a propsed shake-up of the baking and milling industry. Page 31.

After the Finance Sector Union moved yesterday to confirm speculation that 40 per cent of the ANZ Bank's finance company subsidiary Esanda's 1,700 staff would be given redundancy notices this week, ANZ has claimed the union breached a gagging clause by reeasing details of the sackings. The union has refused to rule out retaliatory industrial action. Page 31.
THE AGE

Despite reporting a six per cent fall in full-year profits to A$23.76 million before abnormal costs totalling A$6.89 million, Pacific BBA PBB managing director Barry Jackson says he is optimistic about the company's future, saying yesterday he expects sales rvenue to rise sharply this year, powered by a number of factors, including the start-up of brake export contracts to the United States. Page B1.

Following media speculation yesterday that 40 per cent of ANZ Bank's finance company subsidiary Esanda's 1,700 staff would lose their jobs, the Finance Sector Union moved later that day to confirm the rumours, a move that has prompted ANZ to claim the unin breached a gagging clause by releasing details of the redundancies. Page B1.

Despite delivering a 57 per cent rise in net profit to A$9.13 million thanks to its takeover of Sunbeam Victa last year, GUD managing director Ian Beynon says business is tough, with GUD's traditional product lines of filters, security products and pumps facing declining revenues and scaling down. Page B1.

In a submission to the Industry Commission's inquiry into the automotive industry, Mitsubishi Motors Australia managing director Mike Quinn said Australia's vehicle manufacturing industry would not survive beyond 2010 if the Howard Government continued to cut tariffs on imported cars after the turn of the century. Page B3.

The Colonial Group confirmed last night co-lead managers J.B. Were, Merrill Lynch, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Ord Minnett would be joined by SBC Warburg as lead manager for its public listing in May. It is hoped the float will raise A$400 million in captal for the group. Page B3.

A first-time tax provision of A$15.56 million has taken the gloss off a A$31.12 million December-half profit for Joseph Gutnick's Great Central Mines. The Yandal Belt gold miner's profit for the six months to December more than doubled from A$7.55 million to A$15.56 million after the tax provision. Page B5.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
